title: Minimum Operations to Collect Elements
statement:
You get `nums`, an array of positive integers, and an integer `k`. Each operation pops the element currently at the end of `nums` and places it in your collection.

Return the fewest operations after which the collection holds every integer `1, 2, ..., k` (extra values in the collection do not matter). The input guarantees that all of `1` to `k` appear in `nums`, so this is always possible.
constraints: Every integer from 1 to k appears in nums
notes:
## Intuition

Operations always take from the end, so after `t` operations the collection is exactly the last `t` elements of `nums`. The question becomes: how short can a suffix be while still containing every value from 1 to `k`? The brute force tries every suffix length and scans it; instead, walk backwards once and keep a set of the needed values seen so far. The first moment the set holds `k` values is the answer.

## Approach

1. Start an empty set `collected` and `operations = 0`.
2. Walk `i` from the last index down to 0; each step is one more operation.
3. If `nums[i] <= k`, it is a needed value, so add it to `collected` (a set ignores repeats).
4. As soon as `collected.size === k`, every value 1 to `k` is in hand: return `operations`.
5. The guarantee means the loop always returns; the final line is only a fallback.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 1, 5, 4, 2]`, `k = 2`. Operation 1 takes `2`: `collected = {2}`. Operation 2 takes `4`, too big, ignored. Operation 3 takes `5`, ignored. Operation 4 takes `1`: `collected = {2, 1}`, size 2, so the answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one backward pass with constant-time set operations.
- Space: O(k) for the set.

## Pitfalls

- Only values up to `k` count; adding larger values would make the size check fire too early.
- Duplicates must not be counted twice, which is why a set (not a counter) is used.
- Count operations from the end of the array, not from the start.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `collected` | distinct needed values (1 to `k`) taken so far |
| `operations` | elements removed from the end so far |
| `i` | index of the element being removed |

narration.2: The set will hold the distinct values from 1 to k collected so far.
narration.3: No elements have been removed yet.
narration.5: Remove elements from the end of the array, one at a time.
narration.7: Only values from 1 to k are needed.
narration.8: Add the needed value; a set ignores a value already collected.
narration.10: Have all k needed values been collected?
narration.11: Yes: this is the fewest operations, since removals only go from the end.
narration.14: Not reached for valid inputs, which always contain 1 to k.
